from pymtl3.stdlib.stream      import IStreamDeqAdapterFL, OStreamEnqAdapterFL

class IntMulFL( Component ):

  # Constructor

  def construct( s ):

    # Interface

    s.istream = IStreamIfc( Bits64 )
    s.ostream = OStreamIfc( Bits32 )

    # Queue Adapters

    s.istream_q = IStreamDeqAdapterFL( Bits64 )
    s.ostream_q = OStreamEnqAdapterFL( Bits32 )

    s.istream //= s.istream_q.istream
    s.ostream //= s.ostream_q.ostream

    # FL block

    @update_once
    def block():
      if s.istream_q.deq.rdy() and s.ostream_q.enq.rdy():
        msg = s.istream_q.deq()
        s.ostream_q.enq( msg[32:64] * msg[0:32] )

  # Line tracing

  def line_trace( s ):
    return f"{s.istream}(){s.ostream}"

    12	module lab1_imul_IntMulTrailingZero
    13	(
    14	  input  logic [31:0] in,
    15	  output logic [4:0]  trailing_zeros
    16	);
    17	
    18	  always_comb begin
    19	    trailing_zeros = 5'd0;
    20	    for ( int i = 0; i < 32; i++ ) begin
    21	      if ( in[i] ) begin
    22	        trailing_zeros = i[4:0];
    23	        break;
    24	      end
    25	    end
    26	  end
    27	
    28	endmodule

    34	module lab1_imul_IntMulAltDpath
    35	(
    36	  input  logic        clk,
    37	  input  logic        reset,
    38	
    39	  input  logic [63:0] istream_msg,
    40	  output logic [31:0] ostream_msg,
    41	
    42	  // Control signals from the control unit
    43	
    44	  input  logic        a_mux_sel,
    45	  input  logic        b_mux_sel,
    46	  input  logic        result_mux_sel,
    47	  input  logic        result_en,
    48	
    49	  // Status signals to the control unit
    50	
    51	  output logic        b_is_zero,
    52	  output logic [5:0]  shift_amount,
    53	
    54	  // Internal values exported for line tracing
    55	
    56	  output logic [31:0] a_reg_out,
    57	  output logic [31:0] b_reg_out,
    58	  output logic [31:0] result_reg_out
    59	);
    60	
    61	  //-----------------------------------------------------------------------
    62	  // Determine how far to skip
    63	  //-----------------------------------------------------------------------
    64	
    65	  logic [4:0] trailing_zeros;
    66	
    67	  lab1_imul_IntMulTrailingZero trailing_zero
    68	  (
    69	    .in             (b_reg_out),
    70	    .trailing_zeros (trailing_zeros)
    71	  );
    72	
    73	  assign b_is_zero = (b_reg_out == 32'b0);
    74	
    75	  // Add 1 to the number of trailing zeros
    76	  
    77	  assign shift_amount = {1'b0,trailing_zeros} + 6'd1;
    78	
    79	  //-----------------------------------------------------------------------
    80	  // A operand path
    81	  //-----------------------------------------------------------------------
    82	
    83	  logic [31:0] a_mux_out;
    84	  logic [31:0] a_skip_out;
    85	  logic [31:0] a_shift_out;
    86	
    87	  vc_Mux2#(32) a_mux
    88	  (
    89	    .in0 (istream_msg[63:32]),
    90	    .in1 (a_shift_out),
    91	    .sel (a_mux_sel),
    92	    .out (a_mux_out)
    93	  );
    94	
    95	  always_ff @( posedge clk ) begin
    96	    if ( reset ) a_reg_out <= 32'b0;
    97	    else         a_reg_out <= a_mux_out;
    98	  end
    99	
   100	  // First skip the trailing zeros. This value feeds the result adder.
   101	
   102	  assign a_skip_out = a_reg_out << trailing_zeros;
   103	
   104	  // Then shift past the set bit that was just added. This value feeds
   105	  // back into the A register for the next iteration.
   106	
   107	  assign a_shift_out = a_skip_out << 1;
   108	
   109	  //-----------------------------------------------------------------------
   110	  // B operand path
   111	  //-----------------------------------------------------------------------
   112	
   113	  logic [31:0] b_mux_out;
   114	  logic [31:0] b_shift_out;
   115	
   116	  vc_Mux2#(32) b_mux
   117	  (
   118	    .in0 (istream_msg[31:0]),
   119	    .in1 (b_shift_out),
   120	    .sel (b_mux_sel),
   121	    .out (b_mux_out)
   122	  );
   123	
   124	  always_ff @( posedge clk ) begin
   125	    if ( reset ) b_reg_out <= 32'b0;
   126	    else         b_reg_out <= b_mux_out;
   127	  end
   128	
   129	  // Shift B past the trailing zeros and the set bit that was just added
   130	
   131	  assign b_shift_out = b_reg_out >> shift_amount;
   132	
   133	  //-----------------------------------------------------------------------
   134	  // Result path
   135	  //-----------------------------------------------------------------------
   136	
   137	  logic [31:0] add_out;
   138	  logic [31:0] result_mux_out;
   139	
   140	  assign add_out = a_skip_out + result_reg_out;
   141	
   142	  vc_Mux2#(32) result_mux
   143	  (
   144	    .in0 (32'b0),
   145	    .in1 (add_out),
   146	    .sel (result_mux_sel),
   147	    .out (result_mux_out)
   148	  );
   149	
   150	  always_ff @( posedge clk ) begin
   151	    if      ( reset )     result_reg_out <= 32'b0;
   152	    else if ( result_en ) result_reg_out <= result_mux_out;
   153	  end
   154	
   155	  assign ostream_msg = result_reg_out;
   156	
   157	endmodule

   163	module lab1_imul_IntMulAltCtrl
   164	(
   165	  input  logic       clk,

   175	
   176	  input  logic       b_is_zero,
   177	  input  logic [5:0] shift_amount,

   180	
   181	  output logic       a_mux_sel,

   184	  output logic       result_en,
   185	
   186	  // Internal values exported for line tracing
   187	
   188	  output logic [1:0] status,
   189	  output logic [5:0] counter
   190	);
   191	
   192	  localparam logic [1:0] IDLE = 2'd0;
   193	  localparam logic [1:0] CALC = 2'd1;
   194	  localparam logic [1:0] DONE = 2'd2;
   195	
   196	  logic [1:0] status_next;
   197	  logic [5:0] counter_next;
   198	
   199	  //-----------------------------------------------------------------------
   200	  // State elements
   201	  //-----------------------------------------------------------------------
   202	
   203	  always_ff @( posedge clk ) begin
   204	    if ( reset ) begin
   205	      status  <= IDLE;
   206	      counter <= 6'd0;
   207	    end
   208	    else begin
   209	      status  <= status_next;
   210	      counter <= counter_next;
   211	    end
   212	  end
   213	
   214	  //-----------------------------------------------------------------------
   215	  // State transitions
   216	  //-----------------------------------------------------------------------
   217	
   218	  always_comb begin
   219	    status_next = status;
   220	
   221	    case ( status )
   222	      IDLE: if ( istream_val ) status_next = CALC;
   223	      CALC: begin
   224	        if ( b_is_zero || (counter == 6'd32) ) status_next = DONE;
   225	      end
   226	      DONE: if ( ostream_rdy ) status_next = IDLE;
   227	      default:                 status_next = IDLE;
   228	    endcase
   229	  end
   230	
   231	  //-----------------------------------------------------------------------
   232	  // State outputs
   233	  //-----------------------------------------------------------------------
   234	
   235	  always_comb begin
   236	    istream_rdy    = 1'b0;
   237	    ostream_val    = 1'b0;
   238	    a_mux_sel      = 1'b0;
   239	    b_mux_sel      = 1'b0;
   240	    result_mux_sel = 1'b0;
   241	    result_en      = 1'b0;
   242	    counter_next   = counter;
   243	
   244	    case ( status )
   245	      IDLE: begin
   246	        istream_rdy  = 1'b1;
   247	        result_en    = 1'b1;
   248	        counter_next = 6'd0;
   249	      end
   250	
   251	      CALC: begin
   252	        a_mux_sel      = 1'b1;
   253	        b_mux_sel      = 1'b1;
   254	        result_mux_sel = 1'b1;
   255	
   256	        if ( !b_is_zero && (counter < 6'd32) ) begin
   257	          result_en    = 1'b1;
   258	          counter_next = counter + shift_amount;
   259	        end
   260	      end
   261	
   262	      DONE: begin
   263	        ostream_val = 1'b1;
   264	      end
   265	
   266	      default: begin
   267	        counter_next = 6'd0;
   268	      end
   269	    endcase
   270	  end
   271	
   272	endmodule

    91	// Verilog Components: Drop Unit
    92	//========================================================================
    93	// Drop unit allows dropping a packet when the drop signal is high. This
    94	// is useful especially in pipelined processor, when a squash should drop
    95	// a late arriving memory response.
    96	
    97	`ifndef LAB2_PROC_DROP_UNIT_V
    98	`define LAB2_PROC_DROP_UNIT_V
    99	
   100	module lab2_proc_DropUnit
   101	#(
   102	  parameter p_msg_nbits = 1
   103	)
   104	(
   105	  input  logic                   clk,
   106	  input  logic                   reset,
   107	
   108	  // the drop signal will drop the next arriving packet
   109	
   110	  input  logic                   drop,
   111	
   112	  input  logic [p_msg_nbits-1:0] istream_msg,
   113	  input  logic                   istream_val,
   114	  output logic                   istream_rdy,
   115	
   116	  output logic [p_msg_nbits-1:0] ostream_msg,
   117	  output logic                   ostream_val,
   118	  input  logic                   ostream_rdy
   119	);
   120	
   121	  localparam c_state_pass = 1'b0;
   122	  localparam c_state_drop = 1'b1;
   123	
   124	  logic state;
   125	  logic next_state;
   126	  logic istream_go;
   127	
   128	  assign istream_go = istream_rdy && istream_val;
   129	
   130	  // assign output message same as input message
   131	
   132	  assign ostream_msg = istream_msg;
   133	
   134	  // next state
   135	
   136	  always_comb begin
   137	    if ( state == c_state_pass ) begin
   138	
   139	      // we only go to drop state if there is a drop request and we cannot
   140	      // drop it right away (!istream_en)
   141	      if ( drop && !istream_go )
   142	        next_state = c_state_drop;
   143	      else
   144	        next_state = c_state_pass;
   145	
   146	    end else begin
   147	
   148	      // if we are in the drop mode and a message arrives, we can go back
   149	      // to pass state
   150	      if ( istream_go )
   151	        next_state = c_state_pass;
   152	      else
   153	        next_state = c_state_drop;
   154	
   155	    end
   156	  end
   157	
   158	  // state outputs
   159	
   160	  always_comb begin
   161	    if ( state == c_state_pass ) begin
   162	
   163	      // we combinationally take care of dropping if the packet is already
   164	      // available
   165	      ostream_val = istream_val && !drop;
   166	      istream_rdy  = ostream_rdy;
   167	
   168	    end else begin
   169	
   170	      // we just drop the packet
   171	      ostream_val = 1'b0;
   172	      istream_rdy  = 1'b1;
   173	
   174	    end
   175	  end
   176	
   177	  // state transitions
   178

     4

     7	
     8	`include "vc/trace.v"

    10	`include "lab2_proc/tinyrv2_encoding.v"
    11	
    12	module lab2_proc_ProcBaseCtrl
    13	(
    14	  input  logic        clk,
    15	  input  logic        reset,
    16	
    17	  // Instruction Memory Port
    18	
    19	  output logic        imem_reqstream_val,
    20	  input  logic        imem_reqstream_rdy,
    21	  input  logic        imem_respstream_val,
    22	  output logic        imem_respstream_rdy,
    23	  output logic        imem_respstream_drop,
    24	
    25	  // Data Memory Port
    26	
    27	  output logic        dmem_reqstream_val,
    28	  input  logic        dmem_reqstream_rdy,
    29	  input  logic        dmem_respstream_val,
    30	  output logic        dmem_respstream_rdy,
    31	
    32	  // mngr communication port
    33	
    34	  input  logic        mngr2proc_val,
    35	  output logic        mngr2proc_rdy,
    36	  output logic        proc2mngr_val,
    37	  input  logic        proc2mngr_rdy,
    38	
    39	  // control signals (ctrl->dpath)
    40	
    41	  output logic        reg_en_F,
    42	  output logic [1:0]  pc_sel_F,
    43	
    44	  output logic        reg_en_D,
    45	  output logic [1:0]  op2_sel_D,
    46	  output logic [1:0]  csrr_sel_D,
    47	  output logic [2:0]  imm_type_D,
    48	
    49	  output logic        reg_en_X,
    50	  output logic [3:0]  alu_fn_X,
    51	
    52	  output logic        reg_en_M,
    53	  output logic        wb_result_sel_M,
    54	
    55	  output logic        reg_en_W,
    56	  output logic [4:0]  rf_waddr_W,
    57	  output logic        rf_wen_W,
    58	  output logic        stats_en_wen_W,
    59	
    60	  // status signals (dpath->ctrl)
    61	
    62	  input  logic [31:0] inst_D,
    63	  input  logic        br_cond_eq_X,
    64	
    65	  // extra ports
    66	
    67	  output logic        commit_inst
    68	);
    69	
    70	  //----------------------------------------------------------------------
    71	  // Notes
    72	  //----------------------------------------------------------------------
    73	  // We follow this principle to organize code for each pipeline stage in
    74	  // the control unit.  Register enable logics should always at the
    75	  // beginning. It followed by pipeline registers. Then logic that is not
    76	  // dependent on stall or squash signals. Then logic that is dependent
    77	  // on stall or squash signals. At the end there should be signals meant
    78	  // to be passed to the next stage in the pipeline.
    79	
    80	  //----------------------------------------------------------------------
    81	  // Valid, stall, and squash signals
    82	  //----------------------------------------------------------------------
    83	  // We use valid signal to indicate if the instruction is valid.  An
    84	  // instruction can become invalid because of being squashed or
    85	  // stalled. Notice that invalid instructions are microarchitectural
    86	  // events, they are different from archtectural no-ops. We must be
    87	  // careful about control signals that might change the state of the
    88	  // processor. We should always AND outgoing control signals with valid
    89	  // signal.
    90	
    91	  logic val_F;
    92	  logic val_D;
    93	  logic val_X;
    94	  logic val_M;
    95	  logic val_W;
    96	
    97	  // Managing the stall and squash signals is one of the most important,
    98	  // yet also one of the most complex, aspects of designing a pipelined
    99	  // processor. We will carefully use four signals per stage to manage
   100	  // stalling and squashing: ostall_A, osquash_A, stall_A, and squash_A.
   101	  //
   102	  // We denote the stall signals _originating_ from stage A as
   103	  // ostall_A. For example, if stage A can stall due to a pipeline
   104	  // harzard, then ostall_A would need to factor in the stalling
   105	  // condition for this pipeline harzard.
   106	
   107	  logic ostall_F;  // can ostall due to imem_respstream_val
   108	  logic ostall_D;  // can ostall due to mngr2proc_val or other hazards
   109	  logic ostall_X;  // can ostall due to dmem_reqstream_rdy
   110	  logic ostall_M;  // can ostall due to dmem_respstream_val
   111	  logic ostall_W;  // can ostall due to proc2mngr_rdy
   112	
   113	  // The stall_A signal should be used to indicate when stage A is indeed
   114	  // stalling. stall_A will be a function of ostall_A and all the ostall
   115	  // signals of stages in front of it in the pipeline.
   116	
   117	  logic stall_F;
   118	  logic stall_D;
   119	  logic stall_X;
   120	  logic stall_M;
   121	  logic stall_W;
   122	
   123	  // We denote the squash signals _originating_ from stage A as
   124	  // osquash_A. For example, if stage A needs to squash the stages behind
   125	  // A in the pipeline, then osquash_A would need to factor in this
   126	  // squash condition.
   127	
   128	  logic osquash_D; // can osquash due to unconditional jumps
   129	  logic osquash_X; // can osquash due to taken branches
   130	
   131	  // The squash_A signal should be used to indicate when stage A is being
   132	  // squashed. squash_A will _not_ be a function of osquash_A, since
   133	  // osquash_A means to squash the stages _behind_ A in the pipeline, but
   134	  // not to squash A itself.
   135	
   136	  logic squash_F;
   137	  logic squash_D;
   138	
   139	  //----------------------------------------------------------------------
   140	  // F stage
   141	  //----------------------------------------------------------------------
   142	
   143	  // Register enable logic
   144	
   145	  assign reg_en_F = !stall_F || squash_F;
   146	
   147	  // Pipeline registers
   148	
   149	  always_ff @( posedge clk ) begin
   150	    if ( reset )
   151	      val_F <= 1'b0;
   152	    else if ( reg_en_F )
   153	      val_F <= 1'b1;
   154	  end
   155	
   156	  // forward declaration for PC sel
   157	
   158	  logic       pc_redirect_X;
   159	  logic [1:0] pc_sel_X;
   160	
   161	  // PC select logic
   162	
   163	  always_comb begin
   164	    if ( pc_redirect_X )   // If a branch is taken in X stage
   165	      pc_sel_F = pc_sel_X; // Use pc from X
   166	    else
   167	      pc_sel_F = 2'b0;     // Use pc+4
   168	  end
   169	
   170	  // ostall due to the imem response not valid.
   171	
   172	  assign ostall_F = val_F && !imem_respstream_val;
   173	
   174	  // stall and squash in F
   175	
   176	  assign stall_F  = val_F && ( ostall_F  || ostall_D || ostall_X || ostall_M || ostall_W );
   177	  assign squash_F = val_F && ( osquash_D || osquash_X );
   178	
   179	  // We drop the mem response when we are getting squashed
   180	
   181	  assign imem_respstream_drop = squash_F;
   182	
   183	  // imem is very special. Actually imem requests are sent before the F
   184	  // stage. Note that we need to factor in reset to the imem_reqstream_val
   185	  // signal because we don't want to send out imem request when we are
   186	  // resetting.
   187	
   188	  assign imem_reqstream_val  = ( !stall_F || squash_F ) && !reset;
   189	  assign imem_respstream_rdy = !stall_F || squash_F;
   190	
   191	  // Valid signal for the next stage (stage D)
   192	
   193	  logic  next_val_F;
   194	  assign next_val_F = val_F && !stall_F && !squash_F;
   195	
   196	  //----------------------------------------------------------------------
   197	  // D stage
   198	  //----------------------------------------------------------------------
   199	
   200	  // Register enable logic
   201	
   202	  assign reg_en_D = !stall_D || squash_D;
   203	
   204	  // Pipline registers
   205	
   206	  always_ff @( posedge clk ) begin
   207	    if ( reset )
   208	      val_D <= 1'b0;
   209	    else if ( reg_en_D )
   210	      val_D <= next_val_F;
   211	  end
   212	
   213	  // Parse instruction fields
   214	
   215	  logic   [4:0] inst_rd_D;
   216	  logic   [4:0] inst_rs1_D;
   217	  logic   [4:0] inst_rs2_D;
   218	  logic   [11:0] inst_csr_D;
   219	
   220	  lab2_proc_tinyrv2_encoding_InstUnpack inst_unpack
   221	  (
   222	    .inst     (inst_D),
   223	    .opcode   (),
   224	    .rd       (inst_rd_D),
   225	    .rs1      (inst_rs1_D),

   454	  //----------------------------------------------------------------------

   456	  // Register enable logic

   458	  assign reg_en_X = !stall_X;

   567	  // Valid signal for the next stage

     4	# This module encapsulates the encoding of the TinyRV2 instruction set and
     5	# includes assembly/disassembly functions. We first define a TinyRV2
     6	# encoding table which includes instruction templates and opcode
     7	# mask/match bits. We then define assembly/dissassembly functions for
     8	# each field. Finally, we use the encoding table and assembly/disassembly
     9	# field functions to create the assembly/disassembly instructions for
    10	# single instructions and as well as for small programs.

    12	# Author : Christopher Batten, Shunning Jiang
    13	# Date   : Aug 27, 2016

    21	# Encoding Table
    22	#=========================================================================
    23	# There should be one row in the table for each instruction. The row
    24	# should have three columns corresponding to: instruction template,
    25	# opcode mask, and opcode match. The instruction template should start
    26	# with the instruction name and a list of field tags deliminted by
    27	# whitespace, commas, and/or parentheses. The field tags should map to
    28	# assemble_field and disasm_field functions below. The instruction
    29	# template is used both for assembly and disassembly. The opcode
    30	# mask/match columns are used for decoding; effectively an encoded
    31	# instruction is tested against each entry in the table by first applying
    32	# the mask and then checking for a match.
    33	
    34	# NOTE: We have commented out the subword load/stores since these are not
    35	# currently implemented in the RTL processor. If we have them in the
    36	# ProcFL model but not the RTL model, then code can work on ProcFL but
    37	# then fail in confusing ways on the RTL model. We would rather the code
    38	# fail with an illegal instruction when using ProcFL.
